title: Arlington
name: Arlington
metaTitle: Arlington 1031 Exchange Investors | Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Arlington investors trading stadium-district hospitality, assembly-plant supplier industrial, and campus-adjacent multifamily.

sections.html: Arlington's commercial identity is built on large-scale entertainment and manufacturing rather than a conventional office or retail core. AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, the Texas Live! entertainment district, Six Flags Over Texas, and the General Motors Arlington Assembly Plant sit within a few miles of each other, and each pulls a different kind of real estate demand around it. An exchanger unfamiliar with the corridor can easily assume these four demand drivers behave as one market, when in practice each requires its own underwriting approach and its own set of comparable transactions.

sections.heading: Event-District Hospitality Carries a Different Occupancy Pattern Than Standard Lodging
sections.html: Hotels, short-stay rental product, and restaurant space near the stadium district see occupancy driven by the sports and event calendar rather than steady weekday business travel. A rent roll or income statement for this kind of asset should be reviewed against actual event dates rather than a smoothed annual average that can overstate a slow month and understate a game-week spike. A hotel operator's own occupancy reporting, broken out by month against the actual event schedule, is a more reliable diligence document than a single trailing-twelve-month average presented without that context.

sections.heading: Commercial Property Types an Arlington Exchanger Will Find
sections.html:
The property types clustered around the entertainment and manufacturing districts include:

  • hotel and short-stay lodging near the stadium and entertainment district
  • restaurant and retail space inside or adjacent to the Texas Live! development
  • light-industrial and supplier space serving the General Motors assembly plant's supply chain
  • student-oriented multifamily and retail near the University of Texas at Arlington campus
  • standalone net-lease retail along the corridors connecting the stadium district to surrounding neighborhoods

Restaurant and retail space inside the Texas Live! development typically carries percentage-rent terms tied to the tenant's own sales, and confirming those sales figures directly, rather than relying on the development's overall visitor counts, gives a clearer read on a specific unit's performance.

sections.heading: Identification Strategy for Event-Driven Hospitality Versus Manufacturing-Adjacent Industrial
sections.html: An exchanger exiting stadium-district hospitality with an uneven, event-tied income history often benefits from the 200% rule, which allows a broader list that can include steadier manufacturing-supplier industrial space or a DST interest rather than a narrow list of comparable hospitality assets alone. A DST interest spread across multiple markets can also reduce an exchanger's reliance on any single stadium-district event calendar continuing to draw the same volume it has in recent years.

sections.heading: Supplier Contracts Behind Industrial Leases Near the Assembly Plant Need Direct Review
sections.html: Light-industrial space leased to a supplier tied to the assembly plant's production schedule carries a different risk profile than a standard warehouse lease, since the tenant's own contract with the plant, rather than only its lease with the landlord, drives that tenant's ability to keep paying rent. Requesting a summary of that underlying supplier relationship, where the tenant is willing to share it, adds real diligence value beyond the standard rent roll. Where the tenant declines to share that underlying contract, a shorter identification list weighted toward more transparent property types is often the more defensible path.

sections.heading: Coordinating Closing Around a Stadium-District Event Calendar
sections.html: Scheduling a walkthrough, appraisal, or lender site visit near the stadium district should account for game days and major events, since access and traffic patterns change substantially on those dates. Building that into the closing schedule keeps the qualified intermediary, lender, and title company from losing time to an avoidable scheduling conflict. Confirming parking and access logistics for a lender's appraiser in advance also avoids a wasted trip on a day when stadium traffic makes the site difficult to reach on schedule.

faqs.q: How should I evaluate income from a hotel near the Arlington stadium district?
faqs.a: Review it against the actual event calendar for AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, and Texas Live!, since occupancy swings with game days and major events rather than following a steady weekday pattern.

faqs.q: How many properties should I identify if I'm exiting event-driven hospitality near the stadium district?
faqs.a: More than three is common. The 200% rule lets an investor include steadier manufacturing-supplier industrial space or a DST interest as an alternative to relying solely on comparable hospitality assets.

faqs.q: What should I check before buying industrial space leased to a General Motors supplier?
faqs.a: Ask whether the tenant is willing to share a summary of its underlying supply relationship with the plant, since that contract, rather than the lease alone, drives the tenant's ability to keep paying rent.

faqs.q: Does student housing near UT Arlington behave differently than standard multifamily?
faqs.a: Yes. Leasing near a university campus typically follows an academic-year cycle rather than a standard twelve-month lease pattern, and that cycle should be reflected in any rent roll review.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Fort Worth confirm my Arlington property qualifies for exchange treatment?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates documentation, scheduling, and communication among the investor's advisors. Qualification determinations are made by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.

faqs.q: Should I treat Texas Live! restaurant space the same as a standalone restaurant property elsewhere in the metro?
faqs.a: Not without adjusting for percentage-rent terms tied to the tenant's own sales and the development's event-driven visitor pattern, both of which behave differently than a standalone restaurant lease in a conventional retail corridor.

faqs.q: Do lenders underwrite Arlington stadium-district hospitality differently than a conventional hotel purchase?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Lenders typically want month-by-month occupancy tied to the actual event calendar rather than a single trailing average, and requesting that breakdown early keeps underwriting from stalling once the lender's own review begins.
